messages.content: Let's compare the hotels for the California trip before we reserve anything. The dates are August 9 through August 17, 2026: three nights around the northern Orange County beaches, then five nights in San Diego. It is two adults and our 12-year-old.

I’ll price the stays as August 9-12 and August 12-17, with the child entered as age 12. I’ll check that each quoted room explicitly permits three occupants, identify the actual beds or sofa bed, and include hotel taxes, mandatory fees, and parking. Are you comfortable staying a short drive from the beach if that materially lowers the eight-night total?
Yes. We’ll have the rental car, so Costa Mesa is fine for the first stop. I care more about a room that truly sleeps three than being directly across from the beach.

Two Orange County options look practical. Residence Inn Costa Mesa Newport Beach has a one-bedroom suite with one king and a full sofa bed, listed for up to four guests. The refundable rate is $289 nightly. Best Western Plus Newport Mesa Inn has a two-queen room listed for up to four, at $224 nightly with refundable terms. Both results accept two adults plus the 12-year-old rather than merely assuming the third guest can fit.
What are the complete three-night numbers, and how far are they from Newport and Huntington?

Residence Inn comes to $1,062.51: $867 room, $120.51 taxes and mandatory charges, and $75 for three nights of parking. It includes breakfast. Typical drives are about 12-18 minutes to Newport Beach and 20-30 minutes to Huntington Beach outside peak traffic.

Best Western totals $765.41: $672 room and $93.41 taxes and charges. Parking and breakfast are included. It is roughly 10-15 minutes from Newport Beach and 18-28 minutes from Huntington Beach. Neither quote shows a resort or destination fee.
The Best Western sounds obvious on price, but keep the Residence Inn in play because having a separate bedroom and sofa could be useful. What did you find in San Diego?

The two strongest matches are Homewood Suites San Diego Airport-Liberty Station and Kings Inn San Diego. Homewood’s one-bedroom king suite has a king bed plus a full sofa bed and a maximum occupancy of four. Kings Inn’s two-queen room also has a maximum occupancy of four. Both searches explicitly include the 12-year-old.
Give me the five-night totals, including parking. Also, is the sofa bed actually part of the Homewood room description?

Yes. The selected Homewood rate names a one-bedroom king suite with a full-size sofa bed in the living area; it is not relying on a rollaway. Five nights total $1,824.33: $1,470 room, $204.33 taxes and mandatory charges, and $150 parking. Breakfast is included.

Kings Inn totals $1,047.88: $920 room and $127.88 taxes and charges. Self-parking is included, and there is no mandatory resort fee in the quote. Its two queen beds are listed directly in the room category. Breakfast is not included; the on-site restaurant is paid separately.
How do their locations compare for the zoo, Mission Beach, La Jolla, and the airport?

Homewood at Liberty Station is usually about 8-12 minutes from SAN, 12-18 minutes from the zoo and Balboa Park, 15-20 minutes from Mission Beach, and 20-30 minutes from La Jolla. Kings Inn in Mission Valley is about 12-18 minutes from SAN, 8-12 minutes from the zoo, 12-18 minutes from Mission Beach, and 15-25 minutes from La Jolla. Traffic can add substantially to all of those, especially toward La Jolla in the afternoon.
And the cancellation deadlines? I don't want a vague “refundable” label.

Residence Inn can be canceled without penalty through 11:59 p.m. local hotel time on August 7; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. Best Western has the same August 7 deadline and a one-night-plus-tax late cancellation penalty. Homewood is cancelable through 11:59 p.m. on August 10, with one night plus tax afterward. Kings Inn requires cancellation by 6 p.m. local time on August 9; its late penalty is also one night plus tax.
For this trip, breakfast can be the thing we give up in San Diego. Don't eliminate Kings Inn just because it doesn't include it. The free parking and two real beds may matter more over five nights.

Understood. For this comparison I’ll leave Kings Inn fully viable and account for breakfast separately rather than treating its absence as disqualifying. Its lodging advantage over Homewood is $776.45 before buying any breakfasts, so breakfast spending would have to be unusually high to erase the difference.
Build two combinations, one with the suites and one focused on value. Include the rental-car figure we had and show me one clean total for each.

Suite combination: Residence Inn for three nights plus Homewood Suites for five. Lodging, hotel taxes, mandatory charges, and parking total $2,886.84. Adding the current LAX-to-SAN midsize rental estimate of $684.31 gives $3,571.15. The car figure includes rental taxes and the $75 one-way drop charge; fuel, tolls, and optional coverage are excluded.

Value combination: Best Western for three nights plus Kings Inn for five. Lodging and all quoted hotel charges total $1,813.29, with parking included at both hotels. Adding the same rental makes the combined total $2,497.60.
So the value pair is $1,073.55 less overall?

Correct. The rental cost is identical in both, so the entire $1,073.55 difference comes from the hotels and parking. The value pair provides two queen beds at each stop. The suite pair provides a separate bedroom and living area at both stops, with one king and one sofa bed in each suite, plus included breakfast at both hotels.
Does the three-and-five split still make sense geographically, or are we creating a lot of backtracking?

The split remains sensible. LAX to Costa Mesa is commonly 45-75 minutes after pickup, while driving directly to central San Diego would usually add another 75-110 minutes before traffic complications. On August 12, Costa Mesa to either San Diego hotel is roughly 75-110 minutes in lighter traffic; leaving after the morning commute or after lunch would help. Once in San Diego, both hotels keep the five-night sightseeing drives local, and the Monday departure from SAN is straightforward.
Keep both combinations alive. Before we book, confirm that the quoted totals did not leave out parking tax, that sofa-bed linens are provided in the suites, and that none of these rates are prepaid.

The displayed hotel totals include the taxes applied to the quoted room and parking charges; no additional mandatory hotel fee is shown. Residence Inn and Homewood list sofa-bed bedding as available with the suite, though it is sensible to add a request for the linens to be placed in the room before arrival. All four selected rates are pay-at-property refundable rates, not prepaid.

I’ll retain these two booking candidates: the $3,571.15 suite combination and the $2,497.60 value combination, each including the current $684.31 one-way rental estimate. No reservation has been made, and the next decision is whether the suite layout is worth the $1,073.55 difference before the cancellation inventory or rates change.
